llm.summary: This skill is a clearly documented self-hosted speech tool, but users should only point it at a trusted server because audio, text, and voice samples may be sent there and stored there.

dimensions.detail: The default service can be exposed without auth if mapped broadly, but the documentation repeatedly advises localhost binding, bearer tokens, TLS or reverse proxy controls, and private-download blocking for exposed deployments.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses explicit Docker commands, bind mounts, optional GPU access, and optional bearer auth; these are disclosed and proportionate for running a local speech server.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill openly warns that TTS text, audio, voice-cloning samples, staged files, and URL downloads go to the configured TALKIES_URL, and it gives agent-facing limits for shared file staging and model eviction.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Server-side model files, staged uploads, cached URL downloads, and custom voices persist under the server data directory until cleaned up; this is prominently disclosed with cleanup and access-control guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The network calls, transcription, TTS, voice cloning, file staging, Docker setup, and MCP endpoints match the stated speech-service purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to run or use a trusted talkies server. Prefer localhost or HTTPS, enable TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN for anything shared, avoid sending secrets or sensitive media to servers you do not control, clean up staged files and cached URL downloads, and use voice cloning only with explicit speaker consent.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: TTS examples send input text to the configured TALKIES_URL, which is expected for a networked speech synthesis service and is explicitly disclosed as data leaving the host.
[E1] expected: The voice-cloning workflow sends reference voice material to the talkies server, but the artifacts clearly label this as consent-required and appropriate only for trusted/self-controlled deployments.
[E1] expected: Repeated curl examples transmit speech requests to the configured endpoint; this is not hidden exfiltration in context, though it remains a privacy risk if users choose an untrusted endpoint.
